evidence.supports: Primary source: lists Ordinance No. 26-20, a temporary two-year moratorium on data center permits/construction, introduced under the consent agenda's 'Introduction of Ordinances' with public hearing set for October 8, 2026.
evidence.quote: ORDINANCE NO. 26-20: AN ORDINANCE OF THE HOUSTON CITY COUNCIL ESTABLISHING A TEMPORARY TWO-YEAR MORATORIUM ON THE ACCEPTANCE, PROCESSING, APPROVAL, OR ISSUANCE OF PERMITS AS WELL AS CONSTRUCTION, ESTABLISHMENT, AND OPERATION OF DATA CENTERS WITHIN THE CITY LIMITS OF HOUSTON, ALASKA... Council introduces the ordinances and sets public hearing for October 2026.

evidence.supports: Confirms Houston council introduced a two-year data center construction moratorium to be heard October 8, 2026, and provides context on the AIDEA land-transfer dispute driving it.
evidence.quote: Meanwhile, the nearby Houston city council voted unanimously last month to oppose the land transfer. It also introduced a two-year moratorium on the construction of new data centers to be heard at a meeting on Oct. 8.

evidence.supports: Documents the earlier, distinct August 13, 2026 council vote in which a data-center-blocking ordinance failed 4-2, and a councilmember's stated intent to propose a longer-term moratorium while zoning rules are drafted -- background distinguishing that failed measure from the later Ordinance 26-20.
evidence.quote: An ordinance to block data center construction within Houston city limits failed 4-2, with council members Callie Courtney and Lisa Johansen voting yes. ... Brasel said he plans to propose a resolution imposing a long-term moratorium on data center construction while such zoning rules are crafted.

decisions.notes: Verified against the primary Sept. 10, 2026 council agenda (Ordinance No. 26-20, full title matches verbatim), corroborated by Alaska Beacon and the Mat-Su Sentinel's account of the distinct, earlier failed Aug. 13, 2026 measure. 'pending' correct -- introduced, hearing/vote set for Oct. 8, 2026, no adoption yet. No duplicate.
